summary: Elevated TTFB on chat completions after runtime + model upgrades
description:
Issue summary: After a staged runtime upgrade (serving-runtime v2.8.0) and a model catalog refresh that published gpt-open-xxl-v1 (quantized build), multiple customers reported elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) on chat completion endpoints. Impact: Customers experienced higher initial latency and some streaming sessions timed out (~30-45s TTFB spikes), causing degraded UX for chat features. Affected traffic: ~8% of host pool for prod-us-east during rollout window and spillover into us-west.

Timeline: 2026-02-27 03:15 UTC - Runtime v2.8.0 rollout started (canary -> gradual).
2026-02-27 03:42 UTC - First customer complaint from Acme Payments via support web form.
2026-02-27 04:10 UTC - Alerts triggered: 95th percentile TTFB for chat completions in us-east crossed 800ms baseline to ~3.2s.
2026-02-27 04:50 UTC - Engineering rollback of runtime canary to v2.7.6 for affected pools; partial mitigation observed.
2026-02-27 06:30 UTC - Full rollback initiated for prod-us-east; TTFB returned to baseline by 07:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send chat completion request to /v1/chat/completions with long system prompt and temperature 0.7 to endpoint pinned to gpt-open-xxl-v1; 2) Observe TTFB via timing headers X-Request-Start and X-First-Token; 3) Repeat across nodes that were upgraded to v2.8.0.

Observed behavior: Initial token generation delayed (TTFB spikes), subsequent tokens stream normally after first token emitted. Some sessions timed out before first token when prompts were long (>1.5k tokens). Logs show long pauses in the serving runtime during kernel selection/compilation path and frequent cache misses on KV-prefix lookups for cached prompts.

Expected behavior: Baseline TTFB ~300-600ms for this workload; streaming should begin reliably within SLA window.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- serving-runtime logs (node-23, 2026-02-27T03:40:12Z): "[WARN] kernel_fallback: compiled_kernel_not_found -> falling back to generic_attention_impl; compile_time=2100ms"
- model-store access logs: "GET /models/gpt-open-xxl-v1/quantized/checkpoint -> 200 OK; download_latency=120ms"
- telemetry: "kv_cache_hit_rate: 12% (expected > 70%)"
investigation_notes: 03:50 UTC - Initial hypothesis: runtime v2.8.0 compiler path introduced a new kernel selection code path that falls back to slower implementation when precompiled kernels are missing.
04:05 UTC - Observed low KV cache hit rates on upgraded hosts; suspect cache format mismatch after model refresh/quantization changes (prefix keys differ).
04:20 UTC - Canary nodes showed frequent 'compiled_kernel_not_found' warnings and long compile times (~2s) which correlate with elevated TTFB for first token.

04:35 UTC - Confirmed model-store responded normal; model download latency not the primary cause. Model artifacts present but compiled kernels absent for combination of sequence lengths and quantization profile used by gpt-open-xxl-v1.

05:10 UTC - Reproduced locally by deploying v2.8.0 against gpt-open-xxl-v1 with an empty kernel cache: first request triggered on-the-fly kernel compilation and TTFB spike; subsequent requests benefited from compiled kernel cache.
05:45 UTC - Related PRs found: runtime PR #1243 changed kernel cache key namespace; model-store PR #98 updated quantized artifact metadata which changed expected kernel key derivation.
06:00 UTC - Alternative hypothesis: autoscaler created cold hosts with no prewarm step; combined with new runtime behavior this exposed the compile latency.

resolution: Mitigation: Rolled back serving-runtime canary and then fully rolled back prod-us-east to v2.7.6 at 06:30 UTC which returned TTFB to baseline by 07:00 UTC. Root cause: mismatch between the new kernel cache key namespace introduced in v2.8.0 and the metadata format for newly published quantized model artifacts, causing compiled kernels to be missing and triggering on-the-fly compilation for first requests. Fix applied: Reverted kernel key namespace change in runtime and published runtime patch v2.8.1 with backward-compatible key derivation. Model-store team published a patch to add legacy kernel key mappings (PR #98). Deployment: v2.8.1 rolled out to canary 2026-02-28 01:20 UTC, promoted to prod-us-east 2026-02-28 02:10 UTC after prewarm job verified compiled kernels present. Post-deploy metrics show KV cache hit rate >70% and 95p TTFB within baseline.

Add integration test to runtime CI that validates kernel key compatibility with model-store metadata (owner: runtime team)
Update runtime upgrade runbook to include kernel-cache compatibility checks and prewarm checklist (owner: SRE)
Postmortem doc and customer communication draft for affected customers (owner: CS/Support)
Backfill monitoring alert to detect sudden drop in KV cache hit rate and correlate with TTFB spikes (owner: observability)
Coordinate with model ingestion to gate model-publish metadata changes behind compatibility tests (owner: model on-boarding)
